records.title: Formalized functional analysis with semilinear maps
records.venue: DROPS (Schloss Dagstuhl – Leibniz Center for Informatics)
records.authors: Dupuis, Frédéric; Lewis, Robert Y.; Macbeth, Heather
records.abstract: Semilinear maps are a generalization of linear maps between vector spaces where we allow the scalar action to be twisted by a ring homomorphism such as complex conjugation. In particular, this generalization unifies the concepts of linear and conjugate-linear maps. We implement this generalization in Lean’s mathlib library, along with a number of important results in functional analysis which previously were impossible to formalize properly. Specifically, we prove the Fréchet-Riesz representation theorem and the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators generically over real and complex Hilbert spaces. We also show that semilinear maps have applications beyond functional analysis by formalizing the one-dimensional case of a theorem of Dieudonné and Manin that classifies the isocrystals over an algebraically closed field with positive characteristic.

records.title: Formalizing the ∞-Categorical Yoneda Lemma
records.authors: Nikolai Kudasov; Emily Riehl; Jonathan Weinberger
records.abstract: Formalized 1-category theory forms a core component of various libraries of mathematical proofs. However, more sophisticated results in fields from algebraic topology to theoretical physics, where objects have “higher structure,” rely on infinite-dimensional categories in place of 1-dimensional categories, and ∞-category theory has thusfar proved unamenable to computer formalization.

records.title: Formalizing chemical physics using the Lean theorem prover
records.authors: Maxwell P. Bobbin; Samiha Sharlin; Parivash Feyzishendi; An Hong Dang; Catherine M. Wraback; Tyler R. Josephson
records.abstract: Theories in chemical physics can be reconstructed in a formal language using the interactive theorem prover, Lean. Lean’s ability to check math theorems catches faulty logic and reveals hidden assumptions that are missed in informal derivations.

records.title: Unsolvability of the Quintic Formalized in Dependent Type Theory
records.authors: Sophie Bernard; Cyril Cohen; Assia Mahboubi; Pierre-Yves Strub
records.abstract: In this paper, we describe an axiom-free Coq formalization that there does not exists a general method for solving by radicals polynomial equations of degree greater than 4. This development includes a proof of Galois' Theorem of the equivalence between solvable extensions and extensions solvable by radicals. The unsolvability of the general quintic follows from applying this theorem to a well chosen polynomial with unsolvable Galois group.

records.title: The Operator Derivative in Continuous Stochastic Calculus: A Hilbert Energy Space Framework
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.authors: Ramiro Fontes
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the operator derivative framework for continuous stochastic calculus, using Mathlib. The operator derivative D := δ* is defined as the Hilbert space adjoint of the stochastic integral, reducing stochastic calculus to functional analysis. The formalization comprises 4,600+ lines with zero sorry and one axiom (the Bakry-Émery semigroup interpolation theorem). Verified results include: the Clark-Ocone representation, Leibniz rule, product rule, chain rule (polynomial and smooth extension), abstract and concrete Itô formulas, representer rigidity, stochastic volatility obstruction, PRP equivalence with ker(D) ⊆ constants, Gubinelli base-invariance, Leibniz for fractional Brownian motion (all Hurst parameters H ∈ (0,1)), Lp pointwise multiplication via Hölder's inequality, and the complete Gaussian integration-by-parts chain from the Gaussian PDF derivative through Stein's lemma to the Itô correction. The Hilbert space formulation is what makes formalization tractable: the abstract pipeline compiles against Mathlib's existing functional analysis library without requiring filtrations, stopping times, or measure-theoretic martingale theory. This is a companion artifact to the paper "The Operator Derivative in Continuous Stochastic Calculus: A Hilbert Energy Space Framework" (Fontes, 2026). Lean toolchain: leanprover/lean4:v4.29.0-rc6. Verify with: lake build.

records.title: The Bost-Connes Modular Generator as a candidate Hilbert-Pólya Operator, formalized in Lean 4
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.authors: G Six
records.abstract: Companion repository to the paper. The paper studies the modular generator D_∞ = -i · ∂_t log Δ of the Bost-Connes type III_1 factor at the critical KMS state (β = 1), acting on the GNS Hilbert space, as a candidate Hilbert-Pólya operator. We construct a Galerkin approximation chain whose spectra approximate that of D_∞ in the sense made precise by Bögli-Siegl-Tretter spectral exactness, and package the resulting Galerkin-side ingredients into a single named structured type, CCMGalerkinSpectralData, recorded in Lean 4 against a pinned Mathlib revision. The principal result is a transparent conditional reduction: inhabiting CCMGalerkinSpectralData is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis. This work does not claim a closure of the Riemann Hypothesis — no term of CCMGalerkinSpectralData is constructed in the formalization; the Galerkin-side ingredients required for inhabitation are explicitly named in the gate's type-level fields. The chain's canonical terminal HilbertPolyaBostConnes.rh_of_ccm_galerkin (g : CCMGalerkinSpectralData) : RiemannHypothesis is computer-verified against Mathlib's formal statement of the Riemann Hypothesis. The named-axiom budget is closed against literature: 8 CCM-substrate-own atomic axioms (of which 2 — rouche_zero_existence citing Rouché 1862 and collectively_compact_resolvent_uniform_bound citing Anselone 1971 + Stummel 1970 — appear in the canonical terminal's #print axioms closure; 6 are off-terminal background substrate) plus 6 TT-upstream-inherited axioms via Lake-dep on the companion Tomita-Takesaki substrate. Each axiom carries a literature citation whose published proof does not invoke the Riemann Hypothesis; full per-axiom disclosure is in the companion axioms-disclosure.md document, with the bibliography in references.tex. Companion Lean 4 formalization: localparty/hilbert-polya-bost-connes-lean (v0.1 release, commit 6d29ee6; Mathlib SHA 5e932f97dd25535344f80f9dd8da3aab83df0fe6; Lake-dep on tt-bost-connes-lean v0.2, Zenodo DOI 10.

records.title: Formalization of Complexity Analysis of the First-order Algorithms for Convex Optimization
records.authors: Chenyi Li; Ziyu Wang; Wanyi He; Yuxuan Wu; Shengyang Xu; Zaiwen Wen
records.abstract: The convergence rate of various first-order optimization algorithms is a pivotal concern within the numerical optimization community, as it directly reflects the efficiency of these algorithms across different optimization problems. Our goal is making a significant step forward in the formal mathematical representation of optimization techniques using the Lean4 theorem prover. We first formalize the gradient for smooth functions and the subgradient for convex functions on a Hilbert space, laying the groundwork for the accurate formalization of algorithmic structures. Then, we extend our contribution by proving several properties of differentiable convex functions that have not yet been formalized in Mathlib. Finally, a comprehensive formalization of these algorithms is presented. These developments are not only noteworthy on their own but also serve as essential precursors to the formalization of a broader spectrum of numerical algorithms and their applications in machine learning as well as many other areas.

records.title: Formalization of Two Fixed-Point Algorithms in Hilbert Spaces
records.authors: Yi Bai; Yantao Li; Jian Ming Yu; Jingwei Liang
records.abstract: Iterative algorithms are fundamental tools for approximating fixed-points of nonexpansive operators in real Hilbert spaces. Among them, Krasnosel'ski\uı--Mann iteration and Halpern iteration are two widely used schemes. In this work, we formalize the convergence of these two fixed-point algorithms in the interactive theorem prover Lean4 based on type dependent theory. To this end, weak convergence and topological properties in the infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space are formalized. Definition and properties of nonexpansive operators are also provided. As a useful tool in convex analysis, we then formalize the Fejér monotone sequence. Building on these foundations, we verify the convergence of both the iteration schemes. Our formalization provides reusable components for machine-checked convergence analysis of fixed-point iterations and theories of convex analysis in real Hilbert spaces. Our code is available at https://github.com/TTony2019/fixed-point-iterations-in-lean.

records.title: The Operator Derivative in Continuous Stochastic Calculus: A Hilbert Energy Space Framework
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.authors: Ramiro Fontes
records.abstract: For a continuous process X with stochastic integral δ_X on a Hilbert energy space H_X, the adjoint D_X := δ_X* defines an operator derivative via E[F · δ_X(u)] = E[⟨D_X F, u⟩]. Unlike the Malliavin derivative — which is defined by partial differentiation on cylindrical functionals and satisfies the chain rule by construction — D_X is defined by adjointness on all of L²(Ω) and carries no algebraic structure a priori. It coincides with the Malliavin derivative if and only if the chain rule holds; the chain rule is a theorem about the process, not an axiom of the definition. This distinction organizes stochastic calculus into two logically independent layers. The representation layer — Clark–Ocone formula, Galtchouk–Kunita–Watanabe projection, variance identity — follows from adjointness alone, without assuming any chain rule, Leibniz rule, Gaussianity, or Markov property. The calculus layer — Leibniz rule, chain rule, Itô formula — requires a cylindrical reduction: an integration-by-parts formula that reduces D_X to partial differentiation through representers κ_i ∈ L²(Ω; H_X). The main new result is a representer rigidity theorem: for a continuous martingale M_t = ∫₀ᵗ σ_s dW_s with stochastic volatility, if the extended energy space admits a cylindrical structure with deterministic representers, then σ must be deterministic. Stochastic volatility thus requires random representers inherited from the Brownian Malliavin derivative. The framework has been formally verified in the Lean 4 proof assistant (5,100+ lines, zero sorry, one axiom) using Mathlib. The Gaussian moment theory is grounded in Mathlib's merged Fernique theorem (IsGaussian.memLp_id, PR #30167) and Gaussian measure infrastructure (ProbabilityTheory.IsGaussian, PR #24900). This constitutes the first formalization of stochastic calculus in any proof assistant.

records.title: Lean-Quantum: Toward AI-Assisted Formalization of Quantum Information
records.authors: Kazumi Kasaura; Kei Tsukamoto; Kento Mori; Risa Mizuno; Takahiro Namatame; Yuta Oriike
records.abstract: Quantum information theory is built on entropic quantities; among them, the sandwiched Rényi relative entropy is a fundamental divergence with various applications, and its data processing inequality (DPI) under quantum channels is a cornerstone result. In this work, we present a Lean 4 library for quantum information, designed as a reusable formal infrastructure for theoretical analysis. As a central demonstration of the library, we formalize the DPI for the sandwiched Rényi relative entropy for positive semidefinite operators on finite-dimensional quantum systems. The library provides a basis-independent operator-theoretic framework for finite-dimensional quantum mechanics compatible with the standard mathematical library Mathlib, including reusable interfaces for finite-dimensional systems, states, channels, tensor products, partial traces, Choi operators, Kraus representations, and Stinespring representations. It also builds infrastructure for noncommutative trace inequalities, including operator monotonicity and convexity via the real continuous functional calculus, block-operator positivity, Hilbert-Schmidt operator spaces, Jensen's operator inequality, generalized perspectives, operator power means, and Lieb-Ando trace inequalities. On top of this framework, we formalize entropy-specific ingredients for the DPI: variational formulas for the sandwiched quasi-entropy via Young and reverse-Young inequalities, tensor-product compatibility of real powers, and Haar measures on unitary groups. Together, these components yield a Lean formalization of the DPI, give strong subadditivity as a corollary, and provide the last missing component needed to complete the Lean formalization of the generalized quantum Stein's lemma. More broadly, the development provides machine-checkable foundations for future formalized and AI-assisted research in quantum information theory.

records.title: thiagomassensini/native-carry-spectral-weyl: v0.39.0 — Canonical camera completion
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.authors: Thiago Motta
records.abstract: This release completes the canonical Hilbert-space passage for the countable all-bases camera atlas. Highlights: adds Infinite/CameraCompletion.lean with 24 new public theorems; proves all real bilinear laws for the strictly positive Finsupp Gram form; equips finitely supported camera coefficients with the intrinsic Gram inner product and norm, without an external camera weight; constructs the all-bases camera Hilbert space as Mathlib canonical completion; proves the completion is complete and the canonical linear-isometric embedding has dense range; proves the embedding preserves the Gram inner product and norm exactly; defines canonical single-camera vectors and recovers gramKernel as their exact inner products; defines the label-bounded camera subspaces, proves their monotonicity and compatible isometric inclusions, and proves the union of their images is dense; updates the public API, README, scope, formalization plan, theorem registry, claim ledger and audit. Scope note: this release closes the second Phase 5 gate: the intrinsic all-bases camera Hilbert completion; it does not identify this space with the standard unweighted camera l2 space; the Kolmogorov/Naimark realization, all-bases POVM, Cauchy family and unbounded Weyl inverse remain subsequent obligations. Audit status: 901 public theorem reports; 51 formal claim records; pinned Lean/Mathlib 4.32 toolchain; GitHub Actions exact-checkout audit passed for commit 84799cfb3b875c66e2c1655489793c5c3e2f1e8a.
